title: The First Disciples and the Wedding at Cana
summary: John the Baptist points out Jesus as the Lamb of God, and two of his disciples, one of them Andrew, follow Jesus and stay with him. Andrew brings his brother Simon, whom Jesus calls Cephas. The next day Jesus finds Philip, who finds Nathanael; Nathanael doubts anything good can come from Nazareth, but calls Jesus Son of God and King of Israel. At a wedding in Cana, the wine runs out, and Jesus has servants fill six stone water jars, and the water becomes wine, his first sign.

title: Cleansing the Temple and Nicodemus
summary: At the Passover Jesus drives sellers and money changers out of the temple with a scourge of small cords, saying 'make not my Father's house an house of merchandise,' and when asked for a sign says, 'Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up,' which John says refers to his body. Nicodemus, a Pharisee and ruler, comes to him by night. Jesus says one must be born again of water and the Spirit to enter the kingdom of God.

title: The Woman at the Well
summary: Passing through Samaria, Jesus, tired, sits at Jacob's well at midday and asks a Samaritan woman for a drink. She is surprised, since Jews have no dealings with Samaritans, and he speaks of living water. He tells her about her five husbands, she calls him a prophet, and he says true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth. When she mentions Messias, he says 'I that speak unto thee am he.' She tells the town, and many Samaritans believe and ask him to stay two days.

title: Healing at Bethesda
summary: At a feast in Jerusalem Jesus comes to the pool of Bethesda, where many sick people lie waiting, and asks a man who has been ill thirty-eight years if he wants to be well; he says he has no one to put him in the water. Jesus tells him to take up his bed and walk, and he does, on the Sabbath, which angers the Jews, who seek to kill Jesus for it and for calling God his Father. Jesus says the Son does what he sees the Father do, and that Moses wrote of him.

title: Bread of Life
summary: After crossing the Sea of Galilee, Jesus sees a great crowd and asks Philip where to buy bread; Andrew points to a boy with five barley loaves and two fish, and Jesus gives thanks and distributes them to about five thousand, with twelve baskets left. That night he walks on the sea to the disciples' boat. Next day in Capernaum he says 'I am the bread of life.' Many disciples leave, and Peter says the twelve have words of eternal life.

title: The Woman Caught in Adultery
summary: The scribes and Pharisees bring Jesus a woman caught in adultery and remind him that Moses commanded such to be stoned, asking what he says. Jesus stoops and writes on the ground, and when they press him he says, 'He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her.' They leave one by one, beginning with the oldest. Jesus says he does not condemn her and tells her to go and sin no more. Many early manuscripts lack this passage.

title: The Man Born Blind
summary: Passing a man blind from birth, Jesus' disciples ask whether he or his parents sinned; Jesus says neither, but that the works of God might be revealed. He makes clay of spittle, anoints the man's eyes and tells him to wash in the pool of Siloam, and the man comes back seeing. The Pharisees question him and his parents, split over whether Jesus is from God since he healed on the Sabbath. The man says, 'one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.' They cast him out; Jesus finds him.

title: The Good Shepherd
summary: Jesus says the shepherd enters by the door and the sheep hear his voice, and that he is the door and the good shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep, unlike a hireling who flees from the wolf. He says he has other sheep not of this fold. At the Feast of Dedication in Solomon's porch, the Jews ask him to say plainly whether he is the Christ; he says his works witness to him and 'I and my Father are one.' They take up stones, but he escapes beyond the Jordan.

title: The Raising of Lazarus
summary: Lazarus of Bethany, brother of Mary and Martha, falls ill, and Jesus waits two days before going to Judaea despite the disciples' fear. Martha says Lazarus would not have died if he had been there; Jesus says, 'I am the resurrection, and the life.' Jesus weeps at the tomb, has the stone taken away, prays, and cries 'Lazarus, come forth'; the man emerges bound in grave clothes. The chief priests and Pharisees gather the council, and Caiaphas says one man should die for the people.

title: Anointing and Triumphal Entry
summary: Six days before the Passover Mary of Bethany anoints Jesus' feet with costly ointment of spikenard and wipes them with her hair, and Judas Iscariot objects; Jesus says she has kept it for his burial. The chief priests also plan to kill Lazarus. The next day crowds with palm branches meet Jesus as he enters Jerusalem on a young ass, crying 'Hosanna.' Some Greeks ask to see him, and he says the hour is come, comparing himself to a grain of wheat that must die.

title: The Last Supper Discourse
summary: At supper before the Passover Jesus girds himself with a towel and washes the disciples' feet, telling Peter that unless he washes him he has no part with him. He says one of them will betray him and gives a sop to Judas, who goes out into the night; he gives a new commandment to love one another and foretells that Peter will deny him. In the long discourse he promises the Comforter and says 'I am the way, the truth, and the life.' Chapter 17 is his prayer.

title: Arrest, Trial and Crucifixion
summary: After praying, Jesus crosses the brook Cedron to a garden where Judas comes with soldiers and officers; Jesus says 'I am he' and they fall back, and Peter cuts off Malchus's ear. Jesus is taken to Annas and Caiaphas, and Peter denies him three times. Before Pilate he says his kingdom is not of this world; the crowd chooses Barabbas. Jesus is scourged, mocked and crucified at Golgotha; he says 'It is finished', and Joseph of Arimathaea and Nicodemus bury him in a new garden tomb.

title: The Resurrection Appearances
summary: Early on the first day of the week Mary Magdalene finds the stone taken away from the tomb and runs to Peter and the other disciple, who find the linen cloths lying in the tomb. Mary weeps outside, sees two angels and then Jesus, whom she takes for the gardener until he says her name. That evening Jesus stands among the disciples behind locked doors. Thomas, absent, says he will not believe unless he touches the wounds; a week later Jesus appears again, and Thomas says, 'My Lord and my God.'

title: Breakfast by the Sea of Tiberias
summary: After the resurrection seven disciples, including Peter, Thomas, Nathanael and the sons of Zebedee, go fishing on the Sea of Tiberias and catch nothing all night. At dawn Jesus stands on the shore and tells them to cast the net on the right side; they catch 153 large fish, and the disciple whom Jesus loved says 'It is the Lord.' Peter swims to shore. After breakfast Jesus asks Peter three times, 'Lovest thou me?', tells him to feed his sheep, and foretells his death.
